channel.title: Carat Capital — The Trade Paper of the Jewelry World
channel.description: Prices, intelligence and analysis from every desk of the stone trade: diamonds, gold and metals, gemstones, watches, auctions, retail and technology.

item.title: Petra Diamonds holders face a share suspension from 2 November
item.description: The London-listed miner says its FY2026 audit is unfinished, so it expects to miss the 31 October deadline for its annual report. It gives no date for trading to resume.

item.title: Newmont reports $1,454 an ounce all-in cost on $4,317 gold
item.description: Its third-quarter all-in sustaining cost fell from $1,621 in the second quarter but rose from $1,303 a year earlier. Newmont improved its full-year cost guidance to $1,520 an ounce.

item.title: Chow Tai Fook names gold-loan gains first in 90–100% profit alert
item.description: The jeweller expects half-year net profit to the end of September to rise by that much. Group retail value fell 0.5% in the July to September quarter, RTHK and on.cc report.

item.title: Zenith opens layoff talks at Le Locle; source says 100 of 196 jobs
item.description: The LVMH watch brand confirmed a mass-layoff consultation to the AWP news agency. An internal source quoted by AWP puts another 101 jobs at risk in its international distribution network.

item.title: Christie's puts HK$26.5m–43m on a Patek Sky Moon in Hong Kong
item.description: The Iconic 40 sale on 25 November marks Christie's 40th year in Asia. A ruby-dial F.P. Journe Tourbillon Souverain carries HK$16 million to HK$32 million, among five named lots.

item.title: De Beers pays 1bn pula into Botswana fund, JCK reports
item.description: The transfer is the initial payment under the 2023 deal, which Botswana said would total P10 billion over 10 years. JCK puts it at about $73 million.

item.title: GJEPC targets $50m in New Zealand as trade pact takes effect
item.description: India's gem and jewellery exports to New Zealand were $25.43 million in FY2025-26, the export council says. New Zealand's foreign ministry says the agreement entered into force on 20 October.

item.title: Paspaley sells through 14 US doors and caps new partners each year
item.description: The Australian pearl house told JCK it is deliberately not in 70 doors. It says it produces about 80% of Australia's South Sea pearls and has retailed its own jewellery for over 35 years.

item.title: Vietnam ends gold jewellery certificate, caps cash deals at VND 5m
item.description: Decree 390/2026 took effect on 16 October, cutting the non-cash line from VND 20 million a day. It also amends raw-gold import licence clauses and closes pending certificate files.

item.title: Sotheby's expects $9m-plus for 30 watches, nearly all first-owner
item.description: A platinum Patek 5374/300P-001 leads at $2.5 million to $5 million in New York on 7 December. Most of the rest are Tiffany-retailed Pateks, several double-signed and new to auction.

item.title: Phillips puts HK$6m–12m on Mark Cho's Journe Résonance
item.description: The Hong Kong sale on 21 and 22 November adds eight independent lots to a Patek group. An early Tourbillon Souverain carries a range of HK$3.9 million to HK$11.6 million.

item.title: Burgundy board says US$50.6m director deals broke an ASX rule
item.description: Three 2025 advance-sale agreements sent rough to Choron BV, controlled by director Anshul Gandhi, without prior shareholder approval. ASX lists Burgundy as long suspended, with three periodic reports overdue.

item.title: De Beers' rough price index falls 20% as sales volume nearly doubles
item.description: Third-quarter output fell 11% to 6.8 million carats as Orapa and Venetia slowed. Rough sales rose 4% to $731m, and 2026 guidance rises to 25–28 million carats with all of Gahcho Kué.

item.title: Swiss watch exports rise 11.7%, a fourth straight monthly gain
item.description: September shipments reached CHF 2,225.9m, FH figures show. The US rose 85.7% and France 128.2%, gains FH ties to a base effect and possible trade reallocation, while China fell 14.2%.

item.title: Gemfields ruby auction raises $52.0m at $564.54 a carat
item.description: Montepuez Ruby Mining sold 92,153 of the 102,099 carats offered, about half February's weight. Gemfields says its Trade Select strategy now sells some grades separately; the next such sale is planned for December.

item.title: Indian gold dealers swing to premiums of up to $7 an ounce
item.description: Lower prices drew festive and wedding buyers, Reuters reported on 16 October; dealers had offered discounts of up to $6 the week before. Several large Indian funds suspended bulk gold ETF subscriptions.

item.title: Court winds up Petra's treasury unit over £5.65m tax claim
item.description: The order came at the 14 October hearing, nine days after Questco was named to run the strategic review. A restructuring accountant joined the board as senior independent director on 13 October.

item.title: India's gold imports fall 81.27% to $1.8bn in September
item.description: Silver imports fell 49.11% to $665.08m, on Commerce Ministry data released 15 October. From April to September, gold imports were down 27.32% at $19.27bn against the same months of 2025.

item.title: India's rough imports rise 65.65% in carats, 15.14% in value
item.description: September's 130.17 lakh carats cost $1.05bn, GJEPC provisional data show. On Carat Capital's division, the average imported carat cost about 30% less than a year earlier.

item.title: Christie's 8.17-carat D/IF ring sells for $243,200, below estimate
item.description: A Graff 7.85-carat D VS1 ring led Jewels Online at $256,000, inside its range. The New York online sale closed 15 October with $9.3m in total, Rapaport reports.

item.title: Census puts September retail sales at $745.0bn, up 0.8%
item.description: Sales were 6.3% above September 2025. A 28 September annual revision restated August at $739.3bn, against $773.9bn first published, and the release carries no jewellery line.

item.title: Namdeb asks Namibia for fresh capital as diamond revenue falls
item.description: Finance minister Ericah Shafudah says Namdeb Holdings proposed a recapitalisation in September. No amount is set, and its chief executive puts revenue 60% below the pre-slump forecast.

item.title: Richemont and Signet are in talks to join the De Beers bid
item.description: Bloomberg and Reuters report both in talks to join the Global Diamond Consortium, the preferred bidder for Anglo American's De Beers stake. Neither investment would necessarily be large.

item.title: Botswana nears a deal to raise its De Beers stake to 25%
item.description: Bloomberg reported on 13 October that the state and the Global Diamond Consortium are close to agreeing ownership shares, lifting Botswana from 15%. A year ago its president wanted a majority.

item.title: GIA will comment on fluorescence on about 3% of reports
item.description: A named spokesman confirms a fourth-quarter announcement before two new comments reach grading reports. Roughly 30% of submitted stones glow enough to be noteworthy, and about a tenth of those glow strongly.

item.title: $1.19bn of gold jewellery carries India's September exports
item.description: Total gem and jewellery shipments rose 9.4% to $2.95 billion, with studded gold up 50.2%. Cut and polished natural diamonds fell 5.4% in dollars while lab-grown polished rose 40.7%.

item.title: NRF forecasts $1.013 trillion of holiday sales, up 4.2%
item.description: The trade body's November and December projection passes a trillion dollars for the first time, against $972 billion last year. Retailers are expected to make 325,000 to 375,000 seasonal hires.

item.title: Middle West Partners completes its purchase of Lugano
item.description: The high-end jeweller leaves Chapter 11 with four of the ten boutiques it had in 2025 open and its interim chief executive made permanent. Six closed during the bankruptcy.

item.title: Rapaport names Yosi Botzer chief technology officer
item.description: The former Perion Network executive takes a company-wide artificial intelligence mandate. It extends across Rapaport's businesses, including the price list the natural diamond trade discounts against.

item.title: HSNY names Gregory Brown its executive director
item.description: The society founded in 1866 hands its education and preservation work to a member of ten years. He succeeds Nicholas Manousos, who led there for more than a decade. Carolina Navarro stays as deputy.
